data.title: ICC CodeClash 2026
data.details:
Overview:

From Coding Fundamentals to Competitive DSA

ICC CodeClash 2026 is a two-stage coding competition designed to challenge participants across programming fundamentals, coding logic, problem-solving, and Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA).

The competition consists of an Online Virtual Coding Round followed by an Offline Final Round. Participants will first compete in Round 1, and qualifying participants will advance to the Final Round.

Important Communication:

After registering for ICC CodeClash 2026 on Unstop, all participants are requested to join the official WhatsApp group for important announcements, round details, instructions, updates, and further communication.

Official WhatsApp Group:
https://chat.whatsapp.com/CbZU0qrnx6s2u6I6Jc2E75

Competition Structure:

ICC CodeClash 2026 will be conducted in two stages:

Round 1 → Qualify → Final Round

Participants will first take part in the Virtual Coding Round. Based on their performance, qualifying participants will advance to the Offline Final Round.

Round 1 – Virtual Coding Round:

Date: 4 October 2026 (Sunday)
Mode: Online / Virtual
Platform: Hack The Future

Round 1 will consist of basic coding and programming problems designed to test participants on:

  • Programming Fundamentals
  • Coding Logic
  • Problem Solving
  • Logical Thinking
  • Coding & Implementation

Participants will be evaluated based on their performance in the coding round.

Qualification for Final Round:

Participants who successfully qualify Round 1 will advance to the Offline Final Round.

Only Round 1 qualifiers will be eligible to participate in the Final Round.

Participation in Round 1 alone does not guarantee entry into the Final Round.

No certificate will be provided for Round 1.

Final Round – Offline Coding Competition:

Date: 9 October 2026 (Friday)
Mode: Offline
Venue: Chandigarh University, Uttar Pradesh

The Final Round will be a time-bound coding competition focused on:

  • Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA)
  • Problem Solving
  • Coding Logic
  • Algorithms
  • Implementation

Qualified participants will compete in an offline coding environment and demonstrate their DSA, coding, and problem-solving skills.

Prizes & Recognition:

Final Round participants will have the opportunity to receive:

  • Exciting Prizes
  • Goodies
  • Coupons
  • Certificates
  • Other Rewards & Recognitions

Detailed prize information will be mentioned separately in the Prize Section.

Participation Process:

  • Register for ICC CodeClash 2026 on Unstop.
  • Join the official WhatsApp group after registration.
  • Participate in the Virtual Coding Round on 4 October 2026.
  • Perform well and qualify Round 1.
  • Qualified participants will advance to the Offline Final Round.
  • Participate in the Final Round on 9 October 2026.
  • Compete for exciting prizes, certificates, goodies, coupons, and other recognitions.

Skills Assessed:

The competition will assess skills including:

  • Programming Fundamentals
  • Coding
  • Problem Solving
  • Logical Thinking
  • Algorithms
  • Data Structures
  • Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA)
  • Competitive Programming
  • Coding & Implementation

Important Dates:

4 October 2026 (Sunday)

Round 1 – Virtual Coding Round
Online via Hack The Future

After Round 1

Evaluation & Qualification of Participants

Qualifying participants will advance to the Final Round.

9 October 2026 (Friday)

Recognition:

Final Round participants will have opportunities for prizes, certificates, goodies, coupons, and other rewards and recognitions.

Detailed information regarding prizes and recognitions will be provided in the Prize Section.

Important Instructions:

  • Participants must follow all rules, instructions, and timelines communicated by the organizers.

data.title: The Liar's Chatroom
data.details:
Uncover the Deceiver in a 48-Hour AI & NLP Kaggle Challenge!

About the Event

Step into The Liar's Chatroom, a fast-paced 48-hour online Kaggle competition where NLP meets digital forensics!

Participants will build an AI model to analyze fictional group-chat conversations, examine verified evidence, and identify which character is lying. Each conversation features four characters (A, B, C, and D), with exactly one character making a statement that contradicts the facts. Using a custom synthetic dataset, your mission is to train a model that spots contradictions with high accuracy.

️ Event Format & Dataset

  • Dataset: Participants receive a custom synthetic dataset containing labeled training data and unlabeled test data.

  • ️ Approach: You may use any Machine Learning or NLP approach—including custom architectures, pretrained models, LLMs, fine-tuning, or rule-based heuristics.

  • Platform: Hosted externally on Kaggle.

Rules & Regulations

  1. Team Size: Compete individually or in teams of up to 4 members.

  2. Submission Limit: Maximum of 5 submissions per team per day on Kaggle.

  3. Submission Format: Predictions must be uploaded in the prescribed CSV format before the deadline.

  4. Fair Play: Manual labeling of the test dataset and sharing predictions/code between competing teams are strictly prohibited.

  5. Code & Methodology Submission: Top-performing teams on the private leaderboard must submit a brief explanation/repository of their methodology and may be asked to present their approach to qualify for prizes.

Evaluation Criteria

  • Primary Metric: Evaluation is based strictly on Classification Accuracy on the dataset.

  • Final Ranking: Official winners are determined by the Private Kaggle Leaderboard following post-competition code verification.

data.title: Deepfake ML Hackathon
data.details:
Event Overview

Dive into the cutting edge of AI ethics and security in this high-intensity machine learning hackathon focused on deepfake detection. Participants will compete to build accurate, efficient, and robust models designed to identify synthetic media. Designed to test technical prowess and ethical AI thinking, this single-round challenge demands originality and precision as you train and optimize models against a provided dataset.

Event Details

  • Mode: Online Submission
  • Scope: External and Internal (Open to all students and professionals)
  • Participation: Individual or Team (Inter-college and inter-specialization teams allowed)
  • Team Size: 1–4 members
  • Dates: October 29 – November 13, 2026 (Final Submission Deadline: November 13, 2026)

Eligibility Criteria:

Open to all students (UG, PG, PhD) and professionals. Prior ML/DL knowledge is recommended but not mandatory.

Event Rules:

  • Only the provided dataset may be used for training (external data is strictly prohibited).
  • Pre-trained models are permitted, but fine-tuning must be executed exclusively on the provided dataset.
  • All work must be original; plagiarism or code theft will result in immediate disqualification.
  • Only one final submission per team is allowed (teams may update their files until the deadline, but only the last upload will be evaluated).
  • Models must be reproducible; incomplete submissions will not be evaluated.

Submission Criteria:

Upload all deliverables to a Google Drive folder and submit the link. The folder must contain:

  • Source Code: Zipped folder or GitHub repository with a README
  • Trained Model Weights: Compatible with PyTorch or TensorFlow
  • Prediction CSV: Model predictions on the test set
  • Detailed Documentation: Covering the approach, architecture, hyperparameters, training process, and challenges
  • Optional: A short 3–5 minute explanatory video

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Accuracy on Test Set: 50%
  • Model Efficiency (inference speed and memory footprint): 20%
  • Generalization & Robustness: 20%
  • Clarity of Documentation: 10%

Additional Information

The problem statement is classified as "Normal" difficulty, requiring foundational machine learning and deep learning knowledge.

data.title: Growth Hack Challenge
data.details:
Overview

Bhaktiwala is a devotional app for Indian families: live darshan, pandit booking, katha streaming, kundli, daily rituals, and AI-enabled consultation with Pandit G, all in one place.

We're opening a live marketing brief to all college students. Over 20 days, you'll take a real product at launch stage and drive installs. 

What You Have to Do

  • Drive a minimum of 10 verified installs through your referral code. 
  • You can also submit (optional) a roadmap to generate more users for Bhaktiwala.

An install counts only when someone downloads the app through your code and runs the kundli feature at least once. A download alone doesn't count. 

Getting your code: register, download the app, sign up, and your unique referral code appears in the 'more' section.

Guidelines

  • Drive installs through any legitimate means - tapping into your network, creating content etc.
  • An install counts only if they are active, that is, they log in and use a feature 
  • You can view people who have registered through the app in the 'More' section.
  • The highest number of downloads would be ranked as 1st, 2nd and 3rd for the cash prizes worth 6k!

data.title: National Young Programmers Olympiad

Overview:

NYPO 2026 – National Young Programmers Olympiad is a national-level technology competition for students from Classes 8 to 12 across India, organised by Polaris School of Technology and Navneet Education. It is designed to test students on logic, problem-solving, creativity and their ability to build with technology and AI. No prior coding knowledge is required to participate.

The Olympiad has two tracks:

  • Junior Track: Classes 8–10
  • Senior Track: Classes 11–12

Students progress through three stages:

  • Coding Aptitude – Logical thinking and problem-solving
  • Video Round – Demonstrate and communicate their approach to an idea
  • Vibecoding – Use code and AI tools to turn ideas into something real

Registered students will receive preparation material, and the difficulty level is designed separately for each track.

Participants can compete for opportunities and rewards including:

  • Amazon HQ Bengaluru Visit + Industry Exposure & Mentorship
  • ₹10 Lakh Cash Prize
  • ₹1 Crore Polaris Scholarship Grant
  • MacBook Air
  • $100K worth of Tech Credits
  • National-level Certificates & Recognition

Other Details

  • Registration Fee: ₹499
  • Eligibility: Classes 8–12
  • Last Date for Phase 1 Registration: 30 September 2026

data.details:
Welcome to the Code-e-Manipal 2.0 - by LearnIT at Manipal University Jaipur (MUJ)!

About the Opportunity:

LearnIT, the official IT club of Manipal University Jaipur (MUJ), proudly presents Code-ए-Manipal 2.0, the second edition of one of MUJ’s flagship hackathons, an exciting offline coding challenge designed to ignite the passion for problem-solving and innovation among its students.

Building on the success of its first edition, Code-ए-Manipal 2.0 brings together innovators, developers, and problem-solvers to ideate, build, and transform bold ideas into impactful solutions. This event is a fantastic opportunity to showcase your technical prowess and collaborative spirit in a competitive yet supportive environment.

Eligibility:

  • Open to all university/college students, with engineering, science and management backgrounds, nationally and internationally.
  • Each team must have 1 – 6 members.
  • Interdisciplinary and inter-college collaboration is encouraged.

Registration:

  • Registration is mandatory for all teams. Only the team leader needs to register on behalf of the entire team.
  • Platform: Unstop
  • Registration Window: September 27th, 2026 (00:00 IST) – October 10th, 2026 (23:59 IST)

Participation Fees:

  • INR 59 per person (MUJ students)
  • INR 89 per person (Non- MUJ students)
  • Mixed Teams: Participants are allowed to make inter college team but all the team member need to be present on the day of offline round if qualified.
  • Fees are non-refundable.
  • The registration fee for round 2 is INR 219 (MUJ students) and INR 250 (Non- MUJ studnets) to be paid only if qualified for round 2 that is the offline round. Only teams with successful registration and fee payment will be eligible for the Round 1 shortlisting process.

Themes / Tracks:

Projects must fall under one of the following tracks:

  • AI/ML
  • HealthTech
  • FinTech/ EdTech
  • Cybersecurity
  • Generative AI & LLMs
  • Multi-Agent Systems
  • Gaming & Immersive Tech
  • Smart City and Infrastructure
  • Open Innovation

Round 1 – Elimination Round:

  • Attempt the 10-question online assessment.
  • Complete the assessment within the 10-minute time limit.
  • Questions cover Programming Fundamentals, Logical Reasoning, CS Fundamentals, and Problem Solving.
  • No negative marking.
  • Participants meeting the required qualification score will be shortlisted for Round 2 – the Offline Hackathon at Manipal University Jaipur.

Shortlisted teams will be notified by October 11, 2026 and invited to the offline round at Manipal University Jaipur.

Offline Event Support:

Manipal University Jaipur will provide:

  • Electricity and Wi-Fi
  • Classrooms and desks
  • Food and refreshments (Lunch and dinner for all the participants on Day 1 and Breakfast the following day for the Finalists)
  • Basic sleeping arrangements (mattresses)
  • Teams may submit requests to room admins for any additional resources needed.

Offline Event Dates (Final Round):

  • Venue: Manipal University Jaipur
  • Dates: October 15– 16, 2026
  • All team members must be physically present for presentation and Q&A.
  • Evaluation will include live demo, pitch, and in-depth questioning by judges.

Results and Prize Distribution:

  • Winners will be announced during the closing ceremony of the event.
  • Goodies and non-monetary prizes will be distributed during the ceremony itself.
  • Any monetary prizes, if applicable, will be processed after the event via official channels and will not be disbursed on the same day.
  • Top-performing projects may also receive incubation support and networking opportunities.

Certification:

  • All participants will receive Certificates of Participation endorsed by Manipal University Jaipur.
  • Finalists will receive Special Recognition Certificates.

Disqualification Rules:

  • Any form of plagiarism, unethical conduct, or rule violation will result in immediate disqualification.
  • Projects must be built by the team members only.
  • Use of GenAI tools must be transparent and limited to ideation or support.
  • Room admins and core team members will actively monitor fairness.

Campus Conduct and Professionalism:

  • Participants must always maintain professional behaviour.
  • Accessing restricted areas or labs without permission is strictly prohibited.
  • This is an inter-collegiate event promoting collaboration, innovation, and mutual respect — treat everyone with courtesy.

data.title: SAARTHI'26
data.details:
Innovate with Purpose. Build for Impact.

SAARTHI’26 is a 48-hour National Level Hackathon organized by the Department of Computer Science & Engineering and Department of Computer Application in collaboration with the IEEE Student Branch, Graphic Era Hill University (GEHU), Dehradun.

Building on the vision of SAARTHI, meaning a companion or guide, the hackathon brings together student innovators, developers, designers, and problem-solvers to identify real-world challenges and build technology-driven solutions with meaningful social and practical impact.

The event is designed as a platform for innovation, collaboration, mentorship, problem-solving, and technology development, bringing together participants from across India.

Event Details:

  • Event: SAARTHI’26
  • Duration: 48 Hours
  • Dates: 31st Oct – 2nd November 2026
  • Venue: Graphic Era Hill University, Dehradun, Uttarakhand
  • Mode: Hybrid – online registration/submission stages followed by an on-site hackathon round
  • Team Size: 2–4 members
  • Organizer: IEEE Student Branch, Graphic Era Hill University (GEHU)
  • Department: Department of Computer Science & Engineering, GEHU

Theme:

SAARTHI focuses on building technology-driven, inclusive, accessible, scalable, and impactful solutions to real-world challenges.

The previous edition of SAARTHI focused specifically on disability-centric innovation, including assistive technology, accessibility, healthcare, inclusive education, IoT, and digital inclusion. The SAARTHI’25 brochure describes the event as a platform for developing solutions supporting persons with disabilities and highlights accessibility, AI, IoT, healthcare, and education as important areas of innovation.

What to Expect:

  • 48 hours of intensive innovation and development
  • Real-world problem-solving and technology development
  • Top 50 teams shortlisted for on-site participation
  • Mentorship and expert guidance
  • Team-based collaboration
  • Technical evaluation and project demonstrations
  • Networking with fellow innovators, mentors, academia, and industry
  • Opportunities to showcase impactful solutions
  • Recognition and prizes for top-performing teams

Innovation Areas:

Participants may explore solutions involving areas such as:

  • Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
  • Assistive Technology
  • Accessibility & Inclusive Technology
  • Healthcare Technology
  • IoT & Smart Systems
  • Web & Mobile Applications
  • Natural Language Processing
  • Computer Vision
  • Inclusive Education
  • Digital Accessibility
  • Multilingual & Accessible Technology
  • Community & Social Impact Solutions
  • Open Innovation

Participants are encouraged to combine technologies and approaches to develop practical, scalable, and impactful solutions.

Team Structure:

  • Each team must consist of 2–4 members.
  • Teams will work collaboratively on their selected/problem statement challenge.
  • Top 50 teams will be shortlisted for on-site participation at Graphic Era Hill University, Dehradun.
  • The event will recognize 3 winning teams and 3 special awards.

Participation Process:

Stage 1 – Registration & Initial Submission — FREE:

Participants register through the official Unstop opportunity and form their teams.

Teams submit their proposed solution according to the prescribed submission requirements and guidelines.

No registration fee is charged for Stage 1.

Stage 2 – Shortlisting:

Submitted solutions are evaluated by the organizing/evaluation team based on factors such as:

  • Problem understanding
  • Innovation
  • Technical feasibility
  • Impact
  • Scalability
  • Implementation approach

The top 50 teams are shortlisted for the on-site round.

Stage 3 – Offline Participation & Payment:

Only the teams shortlisted for the on-site hackathon will be required to complete the offline-round registration/payment process.

  • Offline Round Participation Fee: ₹800 per team
  • The 800 fee is applicable only to teams shortlisted for the offline round.
  • Participants who are not shortlisted for the on-site round will not be required to pay this fee.
  • Payment instructions will be shared with shortlisted teams through the official event communication channels.
  • The offline round will be conducted at Graphic Era Hill University, Dehradun.

Stage 4 – 48-Hour On-Site Hackathon:

Shortlisted teams participate in the 48-hour hackathon at Graphic Era Hill University, Dehradun, where they develop and refine their solutions.

Stage 5 – Final Evaluation & Demonstration:

Teams present and demonstrate their final solutions before the evaluation panel.

Important Guidelines:

  • Stage 1 registration and initial PPT/solution submission are free of charge.
  • A ₹800 per-team fee will be applicable only to participants from teams shortlisted for the on-site round.
  • Shortlisted teams must complete the required payment process within the timeline communicated by the organizers to confirm their participation in the offline round.
  • The payment is for offline/on-site participation only and is not required for the initial online submission round.
  • Participants must register through the official event registration platform.
  • Teams must comply with the prescribed team-size requirements.
  • Participants are expected to submit original work.
  • Solutions should address the given problem statement/challenge and demonstrate meaningful implementation.
  • Teams must follow all submission, evaluation, code-of-conduct, and event guidelines communicated by the organizers.
  • Shortlisted teams must be available for the on-site round at Graphic Era Hill University, Dehradun.
  • Further submission and evaluation instructions will be communicated to registered participants through the official event channels.

Why Participate?:

SAARTHI’26 is more than a coding competition. It is an opportunity to:

  • Build solutions for real-world challenges
  • Work with a multidisciplinary team
  • Receive guidance and mentorship
  • Develop practical technical skills
  • Showcase your project to experts and peers
  • Network with students, developers, mentors, and industry professionals
  • Compete at a national level
  • Gain recognition for innovative solutions

Join SAARTHI’26 and build technology that creates meaningful impact.

data.details:
Note:

Mandatory Registration On: https://techfest.org/competitions/perceptron-hackathonWhatsapp

About:

Perceptron Hackathon 2026 is presented by the IITB-Optiver AI Innovation Lab and invites builders to tackle ten concrete, technically demanding problems spanning efficient AI systems, causal reasoning, financial markets, multi-agent coordination, education, and trustworthy AI. Teams pick one of six themes and then one specific problem within it, and Round 1 is judged purely on the depth and rigor of their technical plan, not a working prototype. Finalists go on to present their built solutions before a joint panel of Optiver and IIT Bombay judges at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia's largest science and technology festival.

Structure:

  • The competition runs in two rounds, with Round 2 as an in-person final at Techfest, IIT Bombay.
  • Eligibility: Open to all students with a valid ID from their educational institution. Cross-institutional teams are encouraged.
  • Team Size: Maximum 3 members per team.
  • Themes & Problems: Teams choose one problem statement from 10 listed across 6 themes:
    • Efficient AI at Scale
    • Cause & Effect in AI Decisions
    • Markets & Trading Intelligence
    • Agents That Compete/Cooperate/Adapt
    • AI That Teaches
    • AI You Can Actually Trust
  • Some themes offer a choice between 2–3 related problems; the team picks exactly one problem as its Round 1 submission.

Round 1 - Online Abstract Submission:

Teams submit a 600–900 word abstract, along with an optional 1-page architecture diagram, covering:

  • The chosen problem and why they selected it.
  • Their understanding of its core technical difficulty.
  • A concrete proposed approach naming specific techniques, tools, and datasets.
  • How they will meet the problem's Minimum Viable bar.
  • Which stretch goals they would attempt.
  • Any novelty/differentiation.
  • Their evaluation plan.
  • Team fit and risks.

No code, results, or working prototypes are required at this stage. Only the Team Leader may submit, and multiple submissions are not accepted.

Midway Check:

Roughly 15 days before the finals, each shortlisted team submits a 1-page progress report confirming they are on track. This is a lightweight, unscored checkpoint to flag teams needing support before final judging.

Round 2 - Finals:

  • 25–30 teams are shortlisted across all themes combined, not per theme, for the in-person finals at IIT Bombay.
  • Teams must bring a working code/prototype demonstrating their Minimum Viable scope and any stretch goals attempted.
  • Round 1 was plan-only, but Round 2 requires an actual functioning build to present and demo to the judges.
  • Each team presents to a joint panel of Optiver and IIT Bombay judges.
  • Scores are normalized across all finalist teams on a common scale.
  • The top 3 teams overall, not per theme, are declared winners.

Timeline:

  • Registration Closes: 15th October 2026
  • Round 1 Submission Deadline: 31st October 2026
  • Shortlist Announcement: 10th November 2026
  • Midway Check: 1st December 2026
  • Finals: 15th–18th December 2026

Rewards And Prizes:

  • Top 3 Winners: INR 2,00,000
  • Certificates: All participants who qualify for Round 2 will receive a certificate.

Build with ByteAsk. Not another demo.

This two-week online challenge runs from 28 September to 11 October 2026, ahead of Build 2026—a 24-hour hackathon planned at IIT Guwahati on 24–25 October.

Pick an eligible public GitHub repository, make a useful contribution using ByteAsk, and open a pull request with your team. Build something the maintainer would actually want.

The top 10 entrants receive direct interviews for ByteAsk’s paid, remote open-source fellowship.

Event page - https://hackyard.org/build2026/byteask

Format

  • Fully Online: Participate from anywhere.
  • Team-Based: Register your team, and any registered team member can open the PR.
  • Duration: Runs 28 September – 11 October 2026.
  • Deadline: PR submissions close on 11 October at 11:59 PM IST.
  • Selection: Winners are selected before 24 October.
  • Results & Presentations: Results are shared with participants before Build 2026, and finalists may be invited to present on stage if the event is held as planned.

Process:

  • Step 1 – Register: Sign up with a personal email at https://forms.gle/Bd4hufWjJzeCxZAj8. After registering, ByteAsk emails you a unique Pro code and setup instructions.
  • Step 2 – Build: Choose an eligible public GitHub repository with at least 100 stars that your team does not own. Use ByteAsk and have a registered team member open the pull request during the challenge window.
  • Step 3 – Submit: Send each PR through the submission form at https://forms.gle/5KTw1xEiahChgtvHA with the PR URL and your team's ByteAsk account email. You may submit more than one PR, but only one valid PR per team counts for challenge milestones. Each PR can be credited to one team only.

Eligibility

  • Open to Everyone: Students, working professionals, and teams are all welcome.
  • Email Requirement: Registration must use a personal email address.
  • Submission Window: The PR must be opened during the challenge window (28 September – 11 October 2026) by a registered member of your team.
  • Repository Criteria: The repository must be public on GitHub, have at least 100 stars, and must not be owned by your team.

Rules

  • Disclosure Rules: Do not mention ByteAsk in an open PR until it merges except when the repository's contribution or AI-assistance rules require disclosure. Always follow the repository's own rules first.
  • Social Media & Video: A team video about your work may be posted at any time and may tag ByteAsk, but must not link an open PR.
  • Quality Standards: Low-effort, spam, or misleading PRs may be penalised or excluded.
  • Disqualification Criteria: A PR is ineligible if the repository maintainer closes it as spam, AI-generated, or low-effort, or blocks the submitting account.
  • Maintainer Respect: The repository maintainer always decides whether to accept your PR. Respect their time and their review process.

Judging

  • Evaluation Criteria: ByteAsk evaluates entries on PR outcomes, maintainer engagement, community interest, and ByteAsk usage.
  • Core Principle: Quality beats quantity. One meaningful, merged contribution outweighs ten shallow ones.

Prizes and Access

Award / Perk Details
1st Place ₹10,000
2nd Place ₹7,000
3rd Place ₹3,000
Fellowship Interviews Top 10 entrants receive direct interviews for ByteAsk's paid remote open-source fellowship. Selected fellows work on real open-source contributions with a stipend of ₹30,000 per month, initially for three months, plus a ByteAsk subscription. (Note: An interview does not guarantee an offer, ByteAsk shares contract terms directly with selected candidates.)
ByteAsk Pro Access Every registrant who redeems their unique code and completes one ByteAsk session of 3–4 prompts receives the $20 ByteAsk Pro plan.

Timeline

Date Event / Milestone
28 September 2026 Challenge opens, registration live
11 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST PR submissions close, Pro codes expire
Before 24 October 2026 Winners selected and results shared
24–25 October 2026 Build 2026, planned at IIT Guwahati

data.title: Kriyova - 24-Hours Hackathon 2026
data.details:
About the Hackathon:

KRIYOVA – PROJECT-Q 24-Hours Hackathon 2026 is a technology and innovation challenge conducted as part of PROJECT-Q – Virtual Lab Ceremony, bringing together students, developers, innovators, and technology enthusiasts to conceptualize, develop, and demonstrate technology-driven solutions to relevant real-world challenges.

The hackathon provides participants with an intensive 24-hour development environment, enabling them to progress from problem identification and ideation to solution development, testing, and demonstration. Participants are encouraged to apply technical knowledge, emerging technologies, and interdisciplinary approaches to develop solutions that demonstrate innovation, practical relevance, technical feasibility, and potential real-world impact.

KRIYOVA emphasizes structured problem-solving, collaborative development, experimentation, and the transformation of ideas into functional and demonstrable solutions.

Theme:

Question. Explore. Create.

Participants are encouraged to identify meaningful challenges and develop innovative, technology-driven solutions addressing contemporary needs.

Solutions may address challenges across Quantum Computing, Cybersecurity, and Climate Technology, with emphasis on clear problem definition, appropriate technological implementation, practical applicability, and potential for further development.

Interdisciplinary solutions combining multiple domains are also encouraged where relevant.

Domains:

Participants may develop solutions in one or more of the following domains:

Quantum Computing:

Participants may explore:

  • Quantum algorithms and applications
  • Quantum simulation and computation
  • Quantum-enhanced solutions
  • Quantum education and accessibility
  • Real-world applications of quantum technologies

Cybersecurity:

Participants may address:

  • Cybersecurity awareness and protection
  • Secure systems and applications
  • Threat detection and prevention
  • Privacy and data protection
  • Digital security and resilience
  • Security-focused technology solutions

Climate Technology:

Participants may develop technology-driven solutions addressing climate and environmental challenges, including:

  • Renewable and clean energy
  • Energy efficiency and optimization
  • Environmental monitoring
  • Sustainable resource management
  • Waste reduction and circular solutions
  • Climate adaptation and resilience
  • Technology-enabled environmental sustainability

Teams may focus on a single domain or develop interdisciplinary solutions combining multiple domains.

Event Flow:

  • Registration & Briefing: Participants complete the registration process and receive information regarding the challenge, event guidelines, evaluation criteria, schedule, and submission requirements.
  • Problem Identification & Ideation: Teams identify a relevant problem and establish the objectives, proposed approach, and intended outcomes of their solution.
  • 24-Hour Development: Teams design, develop, test, and refine their proposed solutions during the designated 24-hour development period.
  • Prototype Demonstration: Teams demonstrate their developed solution and explain its functionality, technical approach, implementation, and practical relevance.
  • Final Presentation & Evaluation: Teams present their solutions before the evaluation panel and respond to questions concerning the problem addressed, technical implementation, innovation, feasibility, impact, and future scope.

Evaluation Criteria:

Projects may be evaluated on:

  • Problem Understanding & Relevance
  • Innovation & Originality
  • Technical Implementation
  • Functionality & Demonstration
  • Feasibility & Practical Applicability
  • User Experience & Usability
  • Potential Impact & Scalability
  • Presentation & Communication

The evaluation process will consider both the quality of the proposed solution and the team's ability to clearly communicate its technical and practical aspects.

Guidelines:

  • Registration Fee: ₹699 per team
  • Team Size: 1–3 participants
  • Each participant may be a member of only one team.
  • Teams may comprise participants from multidisciplinary academic or technical backgrounds.
  • Proposed solutions should be relevant to at least one of the specified domains.
  • Participants may use appropriate programming languages, frameworks, libraries, platforms, APIs, development environments, and other permissible technological resources.
  • All submitted work must be original and developed by the participating team.
  • Plagiarism, unauthorized copying, or submission of substantially pre-existing work may result in disqualification.
  • Teams must comply with the prescribed event schedule, submission requirements, and instructions issued by the organizing committee.
  • Teams must be prepared to demonstrate their solution during the final evaluation.
  • Participants may be required to explain their technical approach, implementation decisions, and future development scope.
  • The decision of the evaluation panel and organizing committee shall be final.

data.title: Low-Level Hackathon
data.details:
About the Event:

Dive beneath the abstraction layer in the Low-Level Hackathon, a systems-focused engineering competition designed to test your mastery of hardware-adjacent software development!

Participants will tackle low-level problem statements spanning operating systems, networking protocols, compilers, systems programming, and binary security. From memory management and process synchronization to custom packet analysis and binary analysis, teams must design, implement, debug, and optimize robust systems close to the metal.

Available Tracks:

  • Operating Systems: Memory management, process scheduling, concurrency, kernel modules.
  • Computer Networks: Custom protocol stacks, raw socket programming, packet filtering.
  • Compilers & Language Systems: AST parsing, IR generation, optimization passes, custom runtimes.
  • Systems Programming: Low-level file I/O, driver interfaces, hardware acceleration.
  • Low-Level Security: Binary analysis, vulnerability exploitation, mitigation mechanisms.

Recommended Tech Stack: Hands-on familiarity with C/C++, Linux environments, terminal tools, Git, gdb/debuggers, build tools (Make/CMake), and computer architecture principles.

Submission Deliverables:

  • Source Code: Repository link (e.g., GitHub/GitLab) with build/compilation instructions.
  • Executables / Binaries: Pre-compiled testable output.
  • Technical Documentation: System architecture description and implementation details.
  • Benchmarks & Demo: Empirical performance metrics, test suites, and a live or recorded functional demonstration.

Rules & Regulations:

  • Team Size: Teams may consist of 1 to 3 members.
  • Original Code: All submitted code and architectures must be created during the official hackathon window (Nov 9th – 13th).
  • Tooling & Libraries: Publicly available documentation, standard libraries, and open-source tooling are permitted unless restricted by specific track guidelines.
  • Live Demos: Teams may be required to deliver a live demonstration of their engineered system to the judging panel.
  • Decisions: All decisions made by the organizing and judging panels are final.

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Correctness: Full compliance with functional track specifications.
  • Performance: Execution efficiency, throughput, latency, and memory footprint.
  • Technical Depth: Rigorous application and low-level understanding.
  • Robustness: Fault tolerance, edge-case handling, and execution stability.
  • Code Quality: System architecture cleanliness, maintainability, and engineering hygiene.
  • Innovation & Demonstration: Novelty of implementation and quality of the functional demonstration.

data.title: Pokerbots
data.details:
About the Event:

Test your algorithmic trading and game theory skills in Pokerbots, a high-stakes algorithmic bot competition!

Teams must code an autonomous Python bot to compete in a custom poker variant designed with modified Texas Hold’em mechanics to prevent the use of public repositories.

Technical & Runtime Constraints:

  • Environment: Python 3.11.
  • Allowed Libraries: Standard Python libraries, NumPy, and SciPy only (no pip installations allowed at runtime).
  • Compute Limits: 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, read-only filesystem, and zero network access.
  • Time Bank: Cumulative time bank per match (~60 seconds for 400 hands) with a hard wall-clock kill. Crashes or exhausted time banks result in match forfeiture.
  • Communication Protocol: Bots operate automatically via a predefined stdin/stdout protocol.

Tournament Structure & Progression:

All matches utilize duplicate deals (playing every deal twice with swapped seats) to mitigate luck and seat advantage.

  • Stage 1 (Swiss Qualifier): Valid bots play 6 rounds of ~200 duplicate deals (400 hands). Match points: 1 for Win, 0.5 for Draw, 0 for Loss.
  • Stage 2 (Top 32 Finals): The top 32 qualifying teams advance to a full round-robin stage (~500 duplicate deals each). Scores reset prior to this stage.
  • Tie-Breakers: Calculated using a capped chips per hand formula.

Rules & Regulations:

  • Team Size: Teams must consist of exactly 2 members. An individual can only be on one team.
  • Submissions: Teams can re-upload/overwrite submissions until November 15th at 23:59 IST. Only the last valid upload counts.
  • Fair Play & Code Review: Code copying, collusion, and network calls are strictly prohibited. Winners' source code will undergo a thorough manual review prior to prize payouts.

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Duplicate Deal Performance: Match points accrued during the Swiss Qualifier and final standings in the round-robin stage.

data.title: Vibe-A-Thon
data.details:
Vibe A Thon - TENET '26 TechFiesta : Code Your Vibe

Got an idea and the skills to build it? Join Vibe-A-Thon, a fast-paced, on-site hackathon where you’ll turn a surprise problem statement into a working digital prototype in just five hours.

Think fast, build smart, and bring your solution to life. You can participate solo or team up with one other person. Once the challenge is revealed, you’ll ideate, design, develop, test, and prepare your prototype for a live demonstration to the judges.

You’re free to choose your technology stack and development tools. The focus is on building a functional solution that addresses the challenge with thoughtful design, practical value, and a clear user experience.

No PowerPoint presentation is required—judges will evaluate your prototype and its demonstration.

Event Details

  • Date: Friday, 23 October 2026
  • Reporting time: 9:30 AM
  • Competition begins: 10:30 AM
  • Event hours: 9:30 AM–5:00 PM
  • Format: On-site, five-hour build sprint
  • Venue: AISSMS Institute of Information Technology, Kennedy Road, Near R.T.O., Pune – 411001, Maharashtra

Who Can Participate?

The event is open to currently enrolled undergraduate and postgraduate students, as well as working professionals.

  • Register solo or in a team of up to two members
  • Cross-college teams are welcome
  • Each participant may join only one team
  • Team members cannot be changed after registration or on the event day

Registration Fee

  • Solo participant: ₹150
  • Team of two: ₹200 per team

Prize Pool

₹5,000 total prize pool

  • 1st Place: ₹3,000, prize, and Certificate of Merit
  • 2nd Place: ₹2,000, prize, and Certificate of Merit
  • All teams: Certificate of Participation

How It Works

  • The problem statement will be revealed at the start of the competition. Organizers will direct teams to select or receive a challenge.
  • Teams will build their solution from scratch during the five-hour sprint.
  • At the beginning of the event, each team must create a new GitHub repository. Previously created or pre-built project repositories cannot be reused.
  • Teams will demonstrate their prototype directly to the judging panel. The demonstration time limit will be announced on the event day.

Judging Criteria

Judges will evaluate:

  • UI/UX: Interface design, usability, and visual quality
  • Functionality: Working features and implementation quality
  • Feasibility: Practicality and real-world relevance
  • Innovation: Originality and creativity
  • Demonstration: Prototype completeness and clarity of explanation

The prototype itself will be the primary basis of evaluation.

What to Bring

Bring a charged laptop and charger. You may set up your development environment, software, and accounts before the event, but the project itself must be built only after the official problem statement is revealed. Teams that violate the rules may be disqualified.

Think Fast. Build Smart. Code Your Vibe.

Part of TENET 2026 | TechFiesta
